title: How can an isosceles triangle be cut into a rectangle?
description: An isosceles triangle is cut along its height into two matching right triangles. One is turned over and joined along the slanting side, which makes a rectangle with the same area as the triangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the height of an isosceles triangle splits it into two matching right triangles that fit together as a rectangle. Watch for students who join them along the wrong sides.

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 7, Sulba Sutras)
video_script.why: The child uses cut and join from the solved example to dissect an isosceles triangle into a rectangle in one cut.
video_script.substitution: Cut along the height, turn one piece over, and join the slanting sides.
video_script.anchor: the book's isosceles triangle ABC with the height AD
video_script.payoff_line: Cut along the altitude and join the two right triangles to make a rectangle

final_answer.value: cut along the altitude and join the two right triangles along their slanting sides to make a rectangle BD by AD
final_answer.spoken: cut along the altitude and join the two right triangles to make a rectangle

maths_rules: isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC, AD perpendicular to BC; triangles ADB and ADC have AB = AC, a common side AD and right angles at D, so BD = DC and they match
turning ADC over and fitting its slanting side onto AB with the ends swapped is a half turn of ADB about the midpoint of AB, which gives a rectangle with sides BD and AD
the acute angles at A and at B add up to 90 degrees, so each corner of the new figure is a right angle
area = BD × AD = 1/2 × BC × AD, the area of the triangle
video_script.design: One isosceles triangle all video: one cut, one piece turned over, one rectangle.
open_questions: The hook says the triangle is cut along the height AD. The figure is not in the extracted text, so AD is taken as the altitude from the apex to BC, as the worklist describes.

narration: <bookmark mark='angles'/>At each end of the slanting side, the two sharp angles meet.
They add up to a right angle, because the angles of a right triangle do.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>Every corner is a right angle. The figure is a rectangle with the sides B D and eigh D.

narration: <bookmark mark='area'/>The sides are B D and eigh D, and B D is half of B C.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>The area is half of B C times eigh D, the same as the triangle.

<bookmark mark='calc'/>The rectangle is three by four, which is twelve. The triangle is half of six times four, also twelve.
